pages.text: The classroom door opened gently. Grandma came in wearing a woolly hat. Today was her visiting day. The friends all rushed over.
Only timid Lala stepped back. It had been so long that Grandma felt unfamiliar. "I... want to sit on Grandma's lap too," Lala said softly.
Grandma patted her knees. "Who will sit first?" The friends sat in turn. Lala hid behind Teacher Bau and peeped out.
Grandma took a wooden flute from her bundle. Its tune filled the classroom. Lala covered both ears and stepped farther back.
The song ended. Grandma put the flute away. Her lap was empty. Lala had not sat there even once.
Lala wiped away tears with the back of a hand, shoulders shaking. The friends had gone into the yard. Only Lala, Grandma, and Teacher Bau remained.
Grandma patted her empty lap again. "Snuggle onto Grandma's lap!" With its blanket, her lap looked soft.
Teacher Bau lowered one knee beside Lala. Without speaking, Teacher Bau gently nudged Lala's back with a palm. Lala's toes moved a little forward.
Lala took one step, then two. Grandma counted. "One, one step! Two, two steps! Three, snuggle onto my lap!" Lala settled there snugly.
Grandma hugged Lala tightly and rubbed cheeks. Even after a long time apart, one sit on her lap brought warmth. Arms around Grandma's neck, Lala whispered, "Snuggle onto Grandma's lap!"
